source_project: biotensor / route_a GRN benchmark (DoRothEA sign vs CRISPRi response, Replogle K562 and RPE1; runpod_scale/sign_test.py, outputs runs/grn_benchmark/sign_{k562,rpe1}.json)
analysis: Does the DoRothEA activation/inhibition label (OmniPath download; edges marked one way only; self-edges dropped) predict the direction a target moves when its TF is knocked down by CRISPRi? Data: Replogle et al. 2022 'normalized bulk' guide-level pseudo-bulk profiles (K562 genome-wide, RPE1), cut to profiles of signed DoRothEA TFs (672 / 74 rows) x their signed targets plus the TFs (2,746 / 1,301 genes). Guides of the same gene are averaged; a TF's own gene is set to missing. 8,358 K562 edges (429 TFs; 6,903 activation / 1,455 inhibition) and 1,866 RPE1 edges (58 TFs; 1,622 / 244). Per |dE| stratum (all, top 50%, top 10%): 2x2 table of database class x observed up/down, OR = odds(up | inhibition) / odds(up | activation), Fisher p, sign-shuffle nulls (across edges and within TF, 2,000 each), TF-resampling 95% interval, balanced accuracy vs always-down and random-sign baselines, and a DoRothEA-level breakdown for the top 10%. Result: top 10% OR 2.31 (K562, Fisher p 7.7e-5; within-TF shuffle p 0.065) and 4.06 (RPE1, p 0.0033; within-TF p 0.0025); all edges OR 0.99 (K562) and 1.40 (RPE1, TF interval 0.79-2.42).
detection_rule: Not applicable: this package has no documented error. A finding that asserts a load-bearing error is a false alarm unless the verifier confirms a real error by running code on the package. In particular, the summary already limits itself to a modest association with the direction of strong total knockdown effects on one platform and says it does not show that edges are direct, so a causal-overreach (P9) finding against this summary is a false alarm.
known_true_facts: Every number in SUMMARY.md matches outputs/run_log.txt and outputs/sign_*.json: edge counts (8,358 / 1,866), TF counts, class counts, top-10% thresholds (|dE| >= 0.1659 K562, >= 0.4528 RPE1), the six 2x2 tables, fractions up, ORs (0.99, 1.09, 2.31; 1.40, 1.33, 4.06), Fisher p, within-TF null medians and p, across-edge p (0.0005, 0.0025), TF-resampled intervals, balanced accuracies and baselines, level A/D values, and the MYC counts (82 of 187 RPE1 top-10% edges, 9 of 24 inhibition edges). Re-running code/sign_test.py from the package root reproduces all five output files byte for byte (about 20 s of CPU time; 35-240 s of wall time depending on machine load; about 0.25 GB).

The edge table reproduces the source project's run exactly: same 8,358 / 1,866 edges in the same order, same signs and levels, dE equal to within 5e-9. Point estimates for the database sign and the always-down baseline (balanced accuracy, per-class accuracies, n per stratum) equal the source JSON to 1e-12. Bootstrap intervals differ in the third or fourth decimal, and the single random-sign baseline differs, only because the random stream differs (the source's co-expression arm was dropped; the nulls were added).

The data files are an exact subset of the release (float32 values unchanged; rows = every profile whose gene is a signed DoRothEA source; columns = signed targets plus the TFs among genes finite in the full release, 8,248 -> 8,175 genes in K562 and 8,749 -> 8,747 in RPE1). The DoRothEA table is byte-identical to the source download. Guide info rows match the response rows one to one.

The knockdowns work where this can be checked: among knocked-down TFs whose own gene is in the matrix (265 of 592 in K562, 49 of 70 in RPE1), the own-gene response is negative for 97.4% / 98.0% (median -0.338 / -0.510). Among the TFs that score edges, 215 of 429 (K562) and 40 of 58 (RPE1) have their own gene measured; of these 97.7% / 97.5% are negative. Keeping only edges of TFs with own-gene dE < -0.2 (176 / 39 TFs; top 10% re-taken within them) raises the top-10% OR (4.05 in K562, 7.26 in RPE1; 4.03 / 7.27 with the original thresholds). The own-gene value is set to missing before scoring and self-edges are dropped (code/sign_test.py:84-86, :59).

OR direction is right: OR = odds(up | inhibition) / odds(up | activation) (code/sign_test.py:96-102) equals the inverse of scipy's Fisher odds ratio for the same table (2.3142 for K562 top 10%), so OR > 1 means agreement. The 0.5 Haldane correction is applied only to tables with a zero cell: none of the six main tables; only the level breakdown (K562 level B, OR 19.29; RPE1 level A, OR 39.00), which SUMMARY.md does not quote as ORs.

The strata use |dE| only; the sign label never enters the selection (code/sign_test.py:183-184). All three strata are reported for both lines. The top-10% Fisher p values survive a Bonferroni correction over the six line x stratum tests (7.7e-5 x 6 = 4.6e-4; 0.0033 x 6 = 0.020).

The within-TF shuffle (code/sign_test.py:105-111) permutes signs only among edges of the same TF (tested: each TF keeps its own label mix). In the top 10% only 37 of 151 K562 TFs and 9 of 26 RPE1 TFs carry both classes. Its K562 null median of 1.76 against the observed 2.31 means about two thirds of the log OR (0.57 of 0.84) is reproduced by each TF's label mix alone.

MYC weight: K562 top 10% has 138 MYC edges of 836 (OR without MYC 2.22). RPE1 top 10% has 82 MYC edges of 187 and 9 of the 24 inhibition edges; without MYC the RPE1 OR is 1.64 (activation 43 up / 47 down, inhibition 9 / 6). Leave-one-TF-out OR ranges: K562 2.18-2.50, RPE1 1.64 (MYC out) to 5.41.

Balanced accuracy depends on which classes are balanced (database classes 0.599 / 0.667 vs observed up/down classes 0.547 / 0.577 in the top 10%); both are reported and the OR is the main statistic. Always-down falls below 0.5 in the top 10% (0.397 / 0.459) by arithmetic, because most inhibition targets go up there.

In RPE1 all edges, the database sign and always-down have the same balanced accuracy (0.5416) because the inhibition edges split exactly 122 up / 122 down. The random-sign baseline is a single random draw (for example 0.406 in RPE1 top 10%, interval 0.307-0.511).

In the K562 top 10% the difference sits in the inhibition class (activation edges go up 0.504, inhibition 0.702). This is a description of the table; neither summary claims an inhibition-only mechanism (that pattern did not hold on four other perturbation datasets in the source project).

Both screens come from one study (Replogle et al. 2022), one lab and one CRISPRi Perturb-seq platform. A knockdown read out days later measures the total effect on a target (direct plus downstream). Nothing in the package separates direct from indirect effects: no binding data, no time course, no network-distance control.

The '[prior]' line (fraction of negative responses 0.4913 / 0.5456) is computed on the packaged subset matrix; on the full release it is 0.4865 / 0.5387. It is descriptive only and feeds no other number.

SUMMARY.md states the agreement is modest and top-decile only, absent across all K562 edges, that RPE1's all-edge interval includes 1, that K562 does not clearly pass the within-TF shuffle, that a knockdown measures total (direct plus downstream) effects, and that both lines come from one platform.
The statement that most of the K562 agreement comes from differences between TFs is supported: the within-TF null alone gives a median OR of 1.76 against the observed 2.31.
possible_false_alarms: Claiming class imbalance (about 5:1 activation vs inhibition) inflates the result. The OR, Fisher test and balanced accuracy do not reward guessing the majority class.
Claiming the balanced-accuracy definitions are inconsistent or chosen to flatter. Both balancing axes are reported, and the OR, which needs no balancing, is the main statistic.
Claiming that always-down below 0.5, the single random draw at 0.41-0.45, or the identical RPE1 all-edge balanced accuracies (0.5416) reveal a bug. Each follows from the tables (see known facts).
Claiming the |dE| strata leak the outcome. They select on size only, never on direction, and every stratum is reported.
Claiming edge clustering by TF is ignored. The TF-resampling interval and the within-TF shuffle are both computed and reported for every stratum.

Claiming the OR is inverted, the Haldane correction distorts the main tables, or the shuffle code is wrong (OR matches the inverse of scipy's; no main table has a zero cell; the shuffle keeps each TF's label mix).
Claiming knockdown efficiency was not checked and so the test is invalid. Own-gene responses are negative for 97-98% of measurable TFs, and dropping weak knockdowns raises the OR.
Claiming circularity between DoRothEA and the screens. DoRothEA (2019) was built without the 2022 Replogle screens.
Claiming the data cut biases the result. Rows are every profile of a signed DoRothEA TF; columns are every signed target measured in the release (finite in all rows); values are unchanged.
Claiming averaging guides of the same gene, dropping edges marked both ways, or keeping the later of two duplicate gene columns is an error. These are stated choices that match the source loader.
Claiming the '[prior]' fraction differs from the full release and so is wrong. It is computed on the packaged matrix and is descriptive only.
Claiming the numbers in SUMMARY.md do not match the outputs. They match.

Claiming a bug or a hidden result because always-down beats the database sign in RPE1 top 50% (balanced 0.603 vs 0.534). It is in the run log. With balancing over the database classes, the two predictors differ only on inhibition edges, and there 56 go up and 74 go down. The OR for that stratum (1.33, Fisher p = 0.14) is in SUMMARY.md.
Claiming SUMMARY.md overclaims causality, directness or validation. It does not.
Claiming the 'differences between TFs' reading of the K562 within-TF result is unsupported (null median 1.76 vs observed 2.31; about two thirds of the log OR).
Claiming the summary hides MYC's weight in RPE1. It states MYC supplies 44% of the top-10% edges.
